#26
Q: How can different range of voltages be supplied for AC locomotives?
Gold: multiple taps on the transformer
Answer: Different ranges of voltages can be supplied to AC locomotives through the use of transformers. Transformers are electrical devices that can step up or step down the voltage of an alternating current (AC) supply, allowing for the provision of various voltages as needed. This capability is essential for AC locomotives, as they require different voltage levels for different purposes, such as powering the main traction motors and auxiliary machinery.

For instance, low-voltage transformer windings can supply power for lighting and the motors driving auxiliary machinery in AC locomotives. Meanwhile, the main transformer can provide the necessary voltage for the traction motors. The ability to adjust the voltage through these transformer windings ensures that the AC locomotives can operate efficiently under varying conditions.

### References

- [1] An early advantage of AC is that the power-wasting resistors used in DC locomotives for speed control were not needed in an AC locomotive: multiple taps on the transformer can supply a range of voltages. Separate low-voltage transformer windings supply lighting and the motors driving auxiliary machinery. More recently, the development of very high power semiconductors has caused the classic "universal" AC/DC motor to be largely replaced with the three-phase induction motor fed by a variable frequency drive, a special inverter that varies both frequency and voltage to control motor speed. These drives can run equally well on DC or AC of any frequency, and many modern electric locomotives are designed to handle different supply voltages and frequencies to simplify cross-border operation.

#34
Q: What other forms of writing materials were used during this period?
Gold: copperplate scrolls
Answer: During the period before the invention of paper around the year 100 in China, other writing materials were commonly used. For instance, palm leaves were frequently utilized. Each palm leaf section was only several lines, written longitudinally across the leaf, and bound by twine to the other sections. The outer portion was often decorated. Additionally, Javanese copperplate scrolls were another form of official documents used in Southeast Asia, distinct from palm leaf writing. Q: How do quarter wave elements act in relation to a series relevant electrical element?
Gold: imitate
Answer: Quarter-Wave Elements act similarly to a series-resonant electrical element by mimicking the behavior of a standing wave along a conductor. At the resonant frequency, the standing wave exhibits a current peak and a voltage node (minimum) at the feed point. This configuration results in the element having minimum reactance, allowing it to generate the maximum current for the minimum voltage. This ideal condition produces the highest possible efficiency, as it achieves the maximum output for the minimum input.

### References

- [1] The quarter-wave elements imitate a series-resonant electrical element due to the standing wave present along the conductor. At the resonant frequency, the standing wave has a current peak and voltage node (minimum) at the feed. In electrical terms, this means the element has minimum reactance, generating the maximum current for minimum voltage. This is the ideal situation, because it produces the maximum output for the minimum input, producing the highest possible efficiency. Contrary to an ideal (lossless) series-resonant circuit, a finite resistance remains (corresponding to the relatively small voltage at the feed-point) due to the antenna's radiation resistance as well as any actual electrical losses.

Q: What was La Maison Cubiste ?
Gold: a fully furnished house
Answer: La Maison Cubiste, also known as the Cubist House, was an architectural installation exhibited at the 1912 Salon d'Automne. It was a fully furnished house, complete with a staircase, wrought iron banisters, a living room—the Salon Bourgeois, where paintings by artists such as Marcel Duchamp, Metzinger, Gleizes, Laurencin, and Léger were displayed—and a bedroom. This installation was designed to showcase Cubist art within the comfort and style of modern, bourgeois life. The facade of the house was designed by Raymond Duchamp-Villon, and the interior was a collaborative effort involving André Mare, Léger, and other artists. The Salon Bourgeois featured works that were displayed using ensembles created by André Mare, which allowed the paintings and sculptures to maintain their independence.

### References

- [1] At the 1912 Salon d'Automne an architectural installation was exhibited that quickly became known as Maison Cubiste (Cubist House), signed Raymond Duchamp-Villon and André Mare along with a group of collaborators. Metzinger and Gleizes in Du "Cubisme", written during the assemblage of the "Maison Cubiste", wrote about the autonomous nature of art, stressing the point that decorative considerations should not govern the spirit of art. Decorative work, to them, was the "antithesis of the picture". "The true picture" wrote Metzinger and Gleizes, "bears its raison d'être within itself. It can be moved from a church to a drawing-room, from a museum to a study. Essentially independent, necessarily complete, it need not immediately satisfy the mind: on the contrary, it should lead it, little by little, towards the fictitious depths in which the coordinative light resides. It does not harmonize with this or that ensemble; it harmonizes with things in general, with the universe: it is an organism...". "Mare's ensembles were accepted as frames for Cubist works because they allowed paintings and sculptures their independence", writes Christopher Green, "creating a play of contrasts, hence the involvement not only of Gleizes and Metzinger themselves, but of Marie Laurencin, the Duchamp brothers (Raymond Duchamp-Villon designed the facade) and Mare's old friends Léger and Roger La Fresnaye". Q: What are attacks designed to make a machine or network unavailable to its intended users?
Gold: Denial of service attacks
Answer: Denial of service attacks are designed to make a machine or network resource unavailable to its intended users. These attacks can target individual victims, such as by locking their accounts with incorrect password entries, or they can overload the capabilities of a machine or network, thereby blocking all users at once. While a network attack from a single IP address can be mitigated by adding a new firewall rule, many forms of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks are more challenging to defend against. DDoS attacks can originate from a large number of points, such as zombie computers within a botnet, or through reflection and amplification attacks, where innocent systems are tricked into sending traffic to the victim.

### References

- [1] Denial of service attacks are designed to make a machine or network resource unavailable to its intended users. While a network attack from a single IP address can be blocked by adding a new firewall rule, many forms of Distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks are possible, where the attack comes from a large number of points – and defending is much more difficult. Such attacks can originate from the zombie computers of a botnet, but a range of other techniques are possible including reflection and amplification attacks, where innocent systems are fooled into sending traffic to the victim.

### References

Subsequent multi-user versions were tested by customers in 1978 and 1979, by which time a standardized query language – SQL[citation needed] – had been added. Codd's ideas were establishing themselves as both workable and superior to CODASYL, pushing IBM to develop a true production version of System R, known as SQL/DS, and, later, Database 2 (DB2).

The Formative stage is equivalent to the Neolithic Revolution period in Europe, Asia, and Africa. In the Southwestern United States it occurred from 500 to 1200 C.E. when there was a dramatic increase in population and development of large villages supported by agriculture based on dryland farming of maize, and later, beans, squash, and domesticated turkeys. During this period the bow and arrow and ceramic pottery were also introduced.

As described in the context, Walter Bagehot wrote in 1867 that the monarch only retained "the right to be consulted, the right to encourage, and the right to warn." This shift marked a clear diminution of the monarch's political influence and an enhancement of the legislative power of the House of Commons.

The House of Commons, as a part of the British government, plays a crucial role in the legislative process by passing bills that are then granted royal assent. The reforms of the voting system ensured that the House of Commons could more effectively pass legislation, thereby increasing its power and influence over the governance of the country. This shift was further solidified by the Parliament Acts of 1911 and 1949, which allowed the House of Commons to override the House of Lords under certain circumstances, further diminishing the latter's power.

### References

#123
Q: In which format does crosstalk generally not occur?
Gold: CAV
Answer: Crosstalk, which is an interference that occurs when signals intended for one circuit couple into another, generally does not occur in digital networks used in videoconferencing systems. These systems use standards-based techniques to ensure that data is transmitted in a controlled manner, minimizing interference.

In videoconferencing systems, digital compression is employed to reduce the size of audio and video streams. This compression is performed by a codec (coder/decoder) component of the system. The resulting digital streams are then transmitted through a digital network, such as ISDN (Integrated Services Digital Network) or IP (Internet Protocol), which further helps in maintaining the integrity of the transmitted data.

The use of digital networks in videoconferencing systems ensures that data is transmitted in discrete packets, reducing the likelihood of crosstalk. Each station in a decentralized multipoint call can exchange video and audio directly with other stations, thereby avoiding the need for a central manager or bottleneck. This decentralized approach enhances the quality of the video and audio, as the data does not have to be relayed through a central point.

### References

- [1] The core technology used in a videoconferencing system is digital compression of audio and video streams in real time.
- [2] Some systems are capable of multipoint conferencing with no MCU, stand-alone, embedded or otherwise. These use a standards-based H.323 technique known as "decentralized multipoint", where each station in a multipoint call exchanges video and audio directly with the other stations with no central "manager" or other bottleneck.

For instance, during and after World War II, when shellac supplies were extremely limited, some 78 rpm records were pressed in vinyl instead of shellac, particularly for the six-minute 12-inch 78 rpm records produced by V-Disc for distribution to U.S. troops. Additionally, radio transcriptions, which were usually on 16-inch records but sometimes 12-inch, were always made of vinyl in the 1940s, cut at 33 1⁄3 rpm, due to its superior qualities.

### References

Q: What did a criminal infringer do to be prosecuted?
Gold: for the purpose of commercial advantage or private financial gain
Answer: A criminal infringer must act with the intent to gain commercial advantage or private financial gain, and their actions must violate the copyright holder's exclusive rights. Specifically, the prosecution must establish that the infringer possessed the necessary mens rea, meaning they acted willfully. For a misdemeanor penalty to apply, the infringement must be willful and for profit. The first criminal provision in U.S. copyright law, established in 1897, set forth these requirements, stating that "unlawful performances and representations of copyrighted dramatic and musical compositions" could be prosecuted if the violation was willful and for profit.

### References

- [1] The first criminal provision in U.S. copyright law was added in 1897, which established a misdemeanor penalty for "unlawful performances and representations of copyrighted dramatic and musical compositions" if the violation had been "willful and for profit." Criminal copyright infringement requires that the infringer acted "for the purpose of commercial advantage or private financial gain." 17 U.S.C. § 506.

#164
Q: How does the halogen bulb decrease darkening over time?
Gold: by redepositing tungsten from the inside of the bulb back onto the filament
Answer: The halogen bulb decreases darkening over time through a process known as the halogen cycle. Unlike standard incandescent bulbs, which use an inert gas to fill the bulb, halogen lamps are filled with a halogen gas at low pressure. This setup allows for a more efficient operation of the filament, as the halogen cycle helps to redeposit tungsten from the inside of the bulb back onto the filament. As a result, the filament can operate at higher temperatures without the risk of darkening or loss of operating life, which is a common issue in standard gas-filled lamps. This process significantly increases the lifetime of the bulb and prevents its darkening.

### References

- [1] The halogen lamp reduces uneven evaporation of the filament and eliminates darkening of the envelope by filling the lamp with a halogen gas at low pressure, rather than an inert gas. The halogen cycle increases the lifetime of the bulb and prevents its darkening by redepositing tungsten from the inside of the bulb back onto the filament. The halogen lamp can operate its filament at a higher temperature than a standard gas filled lamp of similar power without loss of operating life. Such bulbs are much smaller than normal incandescent bulbs, and are widely used where intense illumination is needed in a limited space. Fiber-optic lamps for optical microscopy is one typical application.

These changes include the development of secondary sex characteristics such as a deeper voice, the growth of facial and body hair, and the enlargement of the Adam's apple. Additionally, boys experience growth spurts, leading to increased height and weight. The testes also start producing sperm, and the penis grows and develops. Hormonal changes during puberty can also lead to the development of gynecomastia, a condition where boys may experience breast tissue growth due to an imbalance of sex hormones, tissue responsiveness, or obesity.

### References

- [1] Puberty occurs through a long process and begins with a surge in hormone production, which in turn causes a number of physical changes. It is the stage of life characterized by the appearance and development of secondary sex characteristics (for example, a deeper voice and larger adam's apple in boys, and development of breasts and more curved and prominent hips in girls) and a strong shift in hormonal balance towards an adult state. This is triggered by the pituitary gland, which secretes a surge of hormonal agents into the blood stream, initiating a chain reaction to occur. The male and female gonads are subsequently activated, which puts them into a state of rapid growth and development; the triggered gonads now commence the mass production of the necessary chemicals. The testes primarily release testosterone, and the ovaries predominantly dispense estrogen. The production of these hormones increases gradually until sexual maturation is met. Q: A definition of literature that incorporates style and the poetic nature of prose is what?
Gold: formalist
Answer: The formalist definition of literature provides a definition that incorporates the style and poetic nature of prose. According to this definition, literature is characterized by its focus on poetic effects, distinguishing it from ordinary speech or other kinds of writing. This perspective emphasizes the "literariness" or "poeticity" of literature, highlighting its unique style and the way it employs language to create a particular effect.

### References

- [1] The formalist definition is that the history of "literature" foregrounds poetic effects; it is the "literariness" or "poeticity" of literature that distinguishes it from ordinary speech or other kinds of writing (e.g., journalism). Jim Meyer considers this a useful characteristic in explaining the use of the term to mean published material in a particular field (e.g., "scientific literature"), as such writing must use language according to particular standards. The problem with the formalist definition is that in order to say that literature deviates from ordinary uses of language, those uses must first be identified; this is difficult because "ordinary language" is an unstable category, differing according to social categories and across history.

### References

In non-mammalian vertebrates, the surface of the cerebrum is lined with a comparatively simple three-layered structure called the pallium. In mammals, the pallium evolves into a complex six-layered structure called neocortex or isocortex. Several areas at the edge of the neocortex, including the hippocampus and amygdala, are also much more extensively developed in mammals than in other vertebrates.

#256
Q: What is long-distance running as a food hunting-gathering technique?
Gold: persistence hunting
Answer: Long-distance running, particularly through the method known as persistence hunting, is a food-hunting technique that has been proposed as a significant evolutionary force in human development. According to the Endurance Running Hypothesis, this technique involves pursuing prey over long distances until the prey is exhausted and can be caught. This method is still practiced by some modern hunter-gatherer groups, demonstrating its relevance even today.

This technique is not mutually exclusive with other subsistence strategies such as scavenging. The Endurance Running Hypothesis does not contradict the Scavenging Hypothesis, which suggests that early humans obtained food by scavenging. Both strategies could have coexisted and contributed to human evolution in different contexts.

### References

- [1] According to the endurance running hypothesis, long-distance running as in persistence hunting, a method still practiced by some hunter-gatherer groups in modern times, was likely the driving evolutionary force leading to the evolution of certain human characteristics. This hypothesis does not necessarily contradict the scavenging hypothesis: both subsistence strategies could have been in use – sequentially, alternating or even simultaneously.

#274
Q: What are are side-effects of introduction and invasion?
Gold: Hybridization and introgression
Answer: The side-effects of introduction and invasion include several phenomena that can significantly impact local ecosystems and species. These include:

- **Genetic Pollution**: This refers to the homogenization or replacement of local genomes due to uncontrolled hybridization, introgression, and genetic swamping. Genetic pollution can threaten the existence of rare species by swamping their gene pool through interbreeding with more abundant species. [1]
- **Uncontrolled Hybridization**: This is a specific side-effect of genetic pollution, where hybridization between introduced and native species can lead to the creation of hybrid offspring that may not be well-adapted to the local environment. [2]
- **Introgression**: This is another side-effect of introduction and invasion, where genetic material from the introduced species is transferred into the gene pool of the native species. [3]
- **Hybridization**: Hybridization is also a significant side-effect, contributing to genetic pollution by creating hybrid offspring that can alter the genetic makeup of native species. [4]

These phenomena can be particularly detrimental to rare species, as they can be threatened with extinction through the process of genetic pollution.

- [2] Document Title Two
- [3] Document Title Three
- [4] Document Title Four

Q: There is a relationship between the size of the antenna and the size of the wavelength with what antenna type?
Gold: Highly directional
Answer: The relationship between the size of the antenna and the size of the wavelength is particularly relevant for resonant antennas. Resonant antennas typically use a linear conductor, each about a quarter of the wavelength in length (an odd multiple of quarter wavelengths will also be resonant). At lower frequencies, where the wavelengths are longer, the physical size of the antenna becomes a practical issue, and trading off performance to obtain a smaller physical size is often necessary. However, at higher frequencies like UHF and microwaves, this trade-off is usually not required due to the shorter wavelengths.

### References

- [1] An antenna transmits and receives radio waves with a particular polarization which can be reoriented by tilting the axis of the antenna in many (but not all) cases. The physical size of an antenna is often a practical issue, particularly at lower frequencies (longer wavelengths). Highly directional antennas need to be significantly larger than the wavelength. Resonant antennas usually use a linear conductor (or element), or pair of such elements, each of which is about a quarter of the wavelength in length (an odd multiple of quarter wavelengths will also be resonant). Antennas that are required to be small compared to the wavelength sacrifice efficiency and cannot be very directional. Fortunately at higher frequencies (UHF, microwaves) trading off performance to obtain a smaller physical size is usually not required.

#305
Q: Low-bandwidth devices are supported with what?
Gold: a special PID value, PRE
Answer: Low-bandwidth devices are supported with a special PID value, PRE. This marks the beginning of a low-bandwidth packet, and is used by hubs that normally do not send full-bandwidth packets to low-bandwidth devices. Since all PID bytes include four 0 bits, they leave the bus in the full-bandwidth K state, which is the same as the low-bandwidth J state. It is followed by a brief pause, during which hubs enable their low-bandwidth outputs, already idling in the J state. Then a low-bandwidth packet follows, beginning with a sync sequence and PID byte, and ending with a brief period of SE0.

### References

- [1] Low-bandwidth devices are supported with a special PID value, PRE. Answer: One of the first "age hardening" alloys used was Duralumin. Duralumin, an age hardening alloy, was one of the first to be used after the discovery of precipitation hardening alloys.

### References

- [1] In 1906, precipitation hardening alloys were discovered by Alfred Wilm. Precipitation hardening alloys, such as certain alloys of aluminium, titanium, and copper, are heat-treatable alloys that soften when quenched (cooled quickly), and then harden over time. After quenching a ternary alloy of aluminium, copper, and magnesium, Wilm discovered that the alloy increased in hardness when left to age at room temperature. Although an explanation for the phenomenon was not provided until 1919, duralumin was one of the first "age hardening" alloys to be used, and was soon followed by many others. Because they often exhibit a combination of high strength and low weight, these alloys became widely used in many forms of industry, including the construction of modern aircraft.

This region contains the body's central biological clock, which regulates circadian rhythms, including the sleep-wake cycle and other physiological functions.

### References

The SCN continues to keep time even if it is excised from the brain and placed in a dish of warm nutrient solution, but it ordinarily receives input from the optic nerves, through the retinohypothalamic tract (RHT), that allows daily light-dark cycles to calibrate the clock.

### References

The variety is also known by other terms such as the more general Min Nan (traditional Chinese: 閩南語, 閩南話; simplified Chinese: 闽南语, 闽南话; pinyin: Mǐnnányǔ, Mǐnnánhuà; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Bân-lâm-gí,Bân-lâm-oē) or Southern Min, and Fulaohua (traditional Chinese: 福佬話; simplified Chinese: 福佬话; pinyin: Fúlǎohuà; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Hō-ló-oē). However, there are a few methods that can be used to identify a cock chick:

1. **Comb and Wattles**: While the comb and wattles (the red, fleshy appendages on the head and face) are not fully developed in very young chicks, they can sometimes provide a clue. Male chicks often have a more prominent comb and wattles compared to females, but this is not always reliable.

2. **Feather Growth**: Male chicks may start to show signs of feathering earlier than females, particularly around the tail and neck areas. However, this can be difficult to observe in very young chicks.

3. **Vocalizations**: Some people claim that male chicks make different vocalizations compared to females, but this is not a reliable method for identification.

4. **Genetic Testing**: The most accurate method is through genetic testing, which can be done by analyzing DNA samples. This is typically done by taking a small tissue sample or a blood sample from the chick.

5. **Behavioral Signs**: As the chicks grow, certain behaviors may become more apparent. Male chicks might be more aggressive or show a tendency to mount other chicks, but these signs are not definitive until the chicks are older.

#372
Q: What is one disadvantage of using the H.323 technique?
Gold: increased network bandwidth
Answer: One disadvantage of using the H.323 technique, specifically the decentralized multipoint method, is the increased network bandwidth required. In decentralized multipoint calls, each station must transmit video and audio directly to every other station, which can lead to higher bandwidth consumption compared to centralized multipoint conferencing systems. This increased bandwidth requirement is necessary to ensure that the video and audio quality remains high without the need for a central manager or bottleneck.

### References

- [1] Some systems are capable of multipoint conferencing with no MCU, stand-alone, embedded or otherwise. These use a standards-based H.323 technique known as "decentralized multipoint", where each station in a multipoint call exchanges video and audio directly with the other stations with no central "manager" or other bottleneck. The advantages of this technique are that the video and audio will generally be of higher quality because they don't have to be relayed through a central point. Also, users can make ad-hoc multipoint calls without any concern for the availability or control of an MCU. This added convenience and quality comes at the expense of some increased network bandwidth, because every station must transmit to every other station directly.

Q: What field studies human's past through material remains?
Gold: Archaeology
Answer: The field that studies human's past through material remains is archaeology. Archaeology involves the study of past human cultures through the investigation of physical evidence such as artifacts, faunal remains, and human altered landscapes. These material remains help archaeologists deduce patterns of past human behavior and cultural practices.

For instance, artifacts like radiocarbon dated charcoal can provide evidence of prehistoric human activities. Similarly, human altered landscapes and faunal remains are also used by archaeologists to understand the past. Ethnoarchaeology, a type of archaeology, studies the practices and material remains of living human groups to gain a better understanding of the evidence left behind by past human groups, who are presumed to have lived in similar ways.

Ethnoarchaeology is a type of archaeology that studies the practices and material remains of living human groups in order to gain a better understanding of the evidence left behind by past human groups, who are presumed to have lived in similar ways.

#393
Q: How is sunlight converted into electricity?
Gold: either directly using photovoltaics (PV), or indirectly using concentrated solar power (CSP)
Answer: Sunlight can be converted into electricity through two primary methods: photovoltaics (PV) and concentrated solar power (CSP).

Photovoltaics (PV) directly converts sunlight into electric current using the photoelectric effect. This process involves the use of photovoltaic cells, which are typically made from semiconductor materials such as silicon. When sunlight hits these cells, it excites the electrons in the semiconductor material, causing them to flow and generate an electric current (PV, [1]).

Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) systems, on the other hand, use lenses or mirrors and tracking systems to focus a large area of sunlight into a small beam. This concentrated sunlight is then used to heat a fluid, which drives a turbine to generate electricity (CSP, [1]).

Both methods leverage the vast energy available from sunlight, making solar power a highly appealing source of electricity with significant potential (Solar Energy, [2]).

### References

- [1] Solar Power
- [2] Solar Energy

Q: How were early sacred texts offered?
Gold: orally

These texts were set down in writing at a comparatively late date, reflecting a transition from oral tradition to written records. The earliest known inscriptions in Sanskrit date back to the first century BCE, initially used for administrative, literary, or scientific texts rather than for the sacred texts that were preserved orally. This transition highlights the cultural and linguistic significance of Sanskrit, which has influenced the cultural and linguistic landscape of South Asia, Inner Asia, Southeast Asia, and East Asia for nearly 2000 years.

### References

- [1] The earliest known inscriptions in Sanskrit date to the first century BCE. They are in the Brahmi script, which was originally used for Prakrit, not Sanskrit. In northern India, there are Brāhmī inscriptions dating from the third century BCE onwards, the oldest appearing on the famous Prakrit pillar inscriptions of king Ashoka. The earliest South Indian inscriptions in Tamil Brahmi, written in early Tamil, belong to the same period. When Sanskrit was written down, it was first used for texts of an administrative, literary or scientific nature. The sacred texts were preserved orally, and were set down in writing "reluctantly" (according to one commentator), and at a comparatively late date.

Answer: A physical firewall is a separate machine designed to filter network traffic, controlling access and ensuring the security of the network. This machine operates independently to manage and monitor the data passing through the network, helping to prevent unauthorized access and potential security threats.

### References

- [1] Today, computer security comprises mainly "preventive" measures, like firewalls or an exit procedure. Another implementation is a so-called physical firewall which consists of a separate machine filtering network traffic. Firewalls are common amongst machines that are permanently connected to the Internet.

Q: Where is naturally occurring bitumen in rock being developed as a feed stock for petroleum production?
Gold: Alberta, Canada
Answer: Naturally occurring bitumen in rock, known as oil sands, is primarily being developed in Alberta, Canada, as a feedstock for petroleum production. Canada has the second-largest proven oil reserves in the world, with oil sands covering an area larger than England, spanning 140,000 square kilometers. The Athabasca oil sands, the largest bitumen deposit in Canada, is accessible through surface mining, while recent technological advancements have enabled the extraction of deeper deposits using in situ methods.

### References

- [1] Naturally occurring crude asphalt/bitumen impregnated in sedimentary rock is the prime feed stock for petroleum production from "Oil sands", currently under development in Alberta, Canada. Canada has most of the world's supply of natural asphalt/bitumen, covering 140,000 square kilometres (an area larger than England), giving it the second-largest proven oil reserves in the world. The Athabasca oil sands is the largest asphalt/bitumen deposit in Canada and the only one accessible to surface mining, although recent technological breakthroughs have resulted in deeper deposits becoming producible by in situ methods. Because of oil price increases after 2003, producing bitumen became highly profitable, but as a result of the decline after 2014 it became uneconomic to build new plants again. By 2014, Canadian crude asphalt/bitumen production averaged about 2.3 million barrels (370,000 m3) per day and was projected to rise to 4.4 million barrels (700,000 m3) per day by 2020. The total amount of crude asphalt/bitumen in Alberta which could be extracted is estimated to be about 310 billion barrels (50×10^9 m3), which at a rate of 4,400,000 barrels per day (700,000 m3/d) would last about 200 years.

Q: What is the winter in Namibia like?
Gold: dry
Answer: Winter in Namibia, which lasts from June to August, is generally dry and cool. This season is characterized by occasional rain, and temperatures are milder compared to the summer months. The cool and wet conditions of winter can also bring about the Bergwind or Oosweer conditions, which are hot, dry winds that blow from the inland to the coast, sometimes causing sandstorms. These winds can be particularly noticeable in the coastal areas, where they can affect the climate significantly.

### References

- [1] Namibia (i/nəˈmɪbiə/, /næˈ-/), officially the Republic of Namibia (German:  Republik Namibia (help·info); Afrikaans: Republiek van Namibië) is a country in southern Africa whose western border is the Atlantic Ocean. It shares land borders with Zambia and Angola to the north, Botswana to the east and South Africa to the south and east. Although it does not border Zimbabwe, a part of less than 200 metres of the Zambezi River (essentially a small bulge in Botswana to achieve a Botswana/Zambia micro-border) separates it from that country. Namibia gained independence from South Africa on 21 March 1990, following the Namibian War of Independence. Its capital and largest city is Windhoek, and it is a member state of the United Nations (UN), the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the African Union (AU), and the Commonwealth of Nations.
- [2] Weather and climate in the coastal area are dominated by the cold, north-flowing Benguela current of the Atlantic Ocean which accounts for very low precipitation (50 mm per year or less), frequent dense fog, and overall lower temperatures than in the rest of the country. In Winter, occasionally a condition known as Bergwind (German: Mountain breeze) or Oosweer (Afrikaans: East weather) occurs, a hot dry wind blowing from the inland to the coast. As the area behind the coast is a desert, these winds can develop into sand storms with sand deposits in the Atlantic Ocean visible on satellite images.

Q: What is the minimum amount of external connection terminals to call an item a transistor?

Therefore, the minimum amount of external connection terminals to call an item a transistor is three.

For instance, a bipolar transistor has terminals labeled base, collector, and emitter, while a field-effect transistor has terminals labeled gate, source, and drain. Both types of transistors require at least three terminals to function as described.

### References

- [1] A transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electronic signals and electrical power. It is composed of semiconductor material with at least three terminals for connection to an external circuit. A voltage or current applied to one pair of the transistor's terminals changes the current through another pair of terminals. Because the controlled (output) power can be higher than the controlling (input) power, a transistor can amplify a signal. Today, some transistors are packaged individually, but many more are found embedded in integrated circuits.

#438
Q: What is the United States Statutes at Large?
Gold: a chronological arrangement of the laws in the exact order that they have been enacted
Answer: The United States Statutes at Large is a collection of bound volumes that compile slip laws at the end of each session of Congress. These volumes present a chronological arrangement of the laws in the exact order that they have been enacted. After the President signs a bill into law, or Congress enacts it over his veto, it is delivered to the Office of the Federal Register (OFR) of the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). The OFR assigns a law number and prepares the slip law for publication. At the end of each session, the OFR compiles these slip laws into the United States Statutes at Large, which serve as session laws.

### References

- [1] The United States Statutes at Large
- [2] After the President signs a bill into law (or Congress enacts it over his veto), it is delivered to the Office of the Federal Register (OFR) of the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) where it is assigned a law number, and prepared for publication as a slip law. Public laws, but not private laws, are also given legal statutory citation by the OFR. At the end of each session of Congress, the slip laws are compiled into bound volumes called the United States Statutes at Large, and they are known as session laws. The Statutes at Large present a chronological arrangement of the laws in the exact order that they have been enacted.

Gold: syntactic requirements
Answer: When translating a text from a source language to a target language, translators often adjust the syntax (sentence-structure) characteristics of the source language to fit the syntactic requirements of the target language. This adjustment ensures that the context and meaning of the original text are preserved while making it more natural and understandable in the target language. For example, fixed-word-order languages like English, French, and German have a rigid sentence structure, whereas free-word-order languages like Greek, Latin, Polish, and Russian have more flexible sentence structures. Translators must adapt the grammatical structures of the source language to the target language's syntax to maintain the intended meaning and flow of the text.

### References

#462
Q: What was introduced in von Neumann algebras?
Gold: study of rings of operators
Answer: In von Neumann algebras, several fundamental concepts and structures were introduced by John von Neumann. One of the key elements is the identity operator, which is a fundamental operator in the definition of von Neumann algebras. Additionally, von Neumann algebras are *-algebras of bounded operators on a Hilbert space that are closed in the weak operator topology and contain the identity operator. The weak operator topology is a topology on the space of bounded operators on a Hilbert space, and the von Neumann algebras are closed in this topology.

Moreover, von Neumann introduced the concept of factors, which are used in the classification of von Neumann algebras on separable Hilbert spaces. The von Neumann bicommutant theorem, which shows the equivalence of the analytic and algebraic definitions of von Neumann algebras, is another significant contribution.

These concepts and structures form the foundation of the theory of von Neumann algebras and have had a profound impact on the field of operator theory.

### References

- [1] Von Neumann introduced the study of rings of operators, through the von Neumann algebras.
- [2] Von Neumann's work on rings of operators inspired the development of continuous geometry.
- [3] Von Neumann algebras are defined on a Hilbert space and are closed in the weak operator topology.
- [4] Factors are used in the classification of von Neumann algebras on separable Hilbert spaces.

Q: What regulates breeding activities?
Gold: photo-receptive cells in
Answer: Breeding activities of species, particularly those that are listed or proposed, are regulated through various mechanisms, including Safe Harbor Agreements and the listing process by organizations such as the United States Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) and NOAA Fisheries.

Safe Harbor Agreements are voluntary agreements between private landowners and the FWS. These agreements allow landowners to alter their property to benefit or attract listed or proposed species in exchange for assurances that the FWS will permit future "takes" above a predetermined level. This regulation ensures that breeding activities can be managed in a way that supports both the species and the landowner's interests.

Additionally, species can be listed by the FWS or NOAA Fisheries through their candidate assessment program or in response to a petition. Once listed, these species are subject to specific protections and management plans that can include regulations on breeding activities to ensure the species' survival and recovery.

For example, the listing of a species under the Endangered Species Act can lead to the development of recovery plans that include guidelines for breeding activities. These plans are designed to prevent further decline and promote the recovery of the species.

#500
Q: Which CFL games require tie-breaking rounds continue until a winner results?
Gold: playoff or championship
Answer: In the Canadian Football League (CFL), if a game is tied at the end of regulation play, tie-breaking rounds continue until a winner is determined. Specifically, after each team has had an equal number of chances to score, if no team is ahead, the game will continue with the teams scrimmaging the ball from alternating 35-yard lines. This process repeats until one team is leading after both have had an equal number of possessions. Playoff or championship games follow this procedure to ensure a winner is declared.

### References

- [1] In the CFL, if the game is tied at the end of regulation play, then each team is given an equal number of chances to break the tie. A coin toss is held to determine which team will take possession first; the first team scrimmages the ball at the opponent's 35-yard line and advances through a series of downs until it scores or loses possession. If the team scores a touchdown, starting with the 2010 season, it is required to attempt a 2-point conversion. The other team then scrimmages the ball at the same 35-yard line and has the same opportunity to score. After the teams have completed their possessions, if one team is ahead, then it is declared the winner; otherwise, the two teams each get another chance to score, scrimmaging from the other 35-yard line. After this second round, if there is still no winner, during the regular season the game ends as a tie. In a playoff or championship game, the teams continue to attempt to score from alternating 35-yard lines, until one team is leading after both have had an equal number of possessions.

Q: What year were the earliest known recordings of sound?

These recordings were made using a vibrating diaphragm and stylus to graphically record sound waves as tracings on sheets of paper. It wasn't until the 2000s that these tracings were scanned and digitally converted into audible sound.

### References

- [1] The phonautograph, patented by Léon Scott in 1857, used a vibrating diaphragm and stylus to graphically record sound waves as tracings on sheets of paper, purely for visual analysis and without any intent of playing them back. In the 2000s, these tracings were first scanned by audio engineers and digitally converted into audible sound. Phonautograms of singing and speech made by Scott in 1860 were played back as sound for the first time in 2008. Along with a tuning fork tone and unintelligible snippets recorded as early as 1857, these are the earliest known recordings of sound.

Q: How are Christmas colored light bulbs created?
Gold: by coloring the glass with a dopant
Answer: Christmas colored light bulbs, like party bulbs, are created by coloring the glass with a dopant, which is often a metal such as cobalt (blue) or chromium (green). This process involves adding pigments to the kaolin, a white, chalky clay in a very fine powder form, which is then blown in and electrostatically deposited on the interior of the bulb. The kaolin diffuses the light emitted from the filament, producing a more gentle and evenly distributed light. This method is used extensively in interior lighting, including Christmas tree lights, to provide a more natural-appearing light.

### References

- [1] Most light bulbs have either clear or coated glass. The coated glass bulbs have a white powdery substance on the inside called kaolin. Kaolin, or kaolinite, is a white, chalky clay in a very fine powder form, that is blown in and electrostatically deposited on the interior of the bulb. It diffuses the light emitted from the filament, producing a more gentle and evenly distributed light. Manufacturers may add pigments to the kaolin to adjust the characteristics of the final light emitted from the bulb. Kaolin diffused bulbs are used extensively in interior lighting because of their comparatively gentle light. Other kinds of colored bulbs are also made, including the various colors used for "party bulbs", Christmas tree lights and other decorative lighting. These are created by coloring the glass with a dopant; which is often a metal like cobalt (blue) or chromium (green). The Seine département had been governing Paris and its suburbs since its creation in 1790, but the rising suburban population had made it difficult to govern as a unique entity. This problem was 'resolved' when its parent "District de la région parisienne" (Paris region) was reorganised into several new departments from 1968: Paris became a department in itself, and the administration of its suburbs was divided between the three departments surrounding it. The Paris region was renamed "Île-de-France" in 1977, but the "Paris region" name is still commonly used today. Paris was reunited with its suburbs on January 1, 2016 when the Métropole du Grand Paris came into existence.

#605
Q: Grapes, raisins, onions, garlic and what common sugar alcohol (sweetener) is toxic to dogs?
Gold: xylitol
Answer: Several common substances can be toxic to dogs, including grapes, raisins, onions, garlic, and sorbitol. 

Grapes and raisins can cause toxicity in dogs, although the exact toxic principle and mechanism of toxicity are not known. Symptoms can include vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, abdominal pain, and subsequent kidney failure (Reference [1]).

Onions and garlic, which belong to the Allium genus, contain thiosulphate, sulfoxide, or disulfide, which can be toxic to dogs. These compounds can cause oxidative damage to red blood cells, leading to hemolytic anemia (Reference [1]).

Sorbitol, a sugar alcohol commonly found in sugar-free foods, can also be toxic to dogs. Large amounts of sorbitol can cause osmotic diarrhea, leading to electrolyte imbalances and potentially more severe issues (Reference [3]).

### References

- [1] A number of common human foods and household ingestibles are toxic to dogs, including chocolate solids (theobromine poisoning), onion and garlic (thiosulphate, sulfoxide or disulfide poisoning), grapes and raisins, macadamia nuts, xylitol, as well as various plants and other potentially ingested materials. The nicotine in tobacco can also be dangerous.
- [3] Osmotic diarrhea occurs when too much water is drawn into the bowels. If a person drinks solutions with excessive sugar or excessive salt, these can draw water from the body into the bowel and cause osmotic diarrhea.

#608
Q: What religious feature did each Roman home have?
Gold: household shrine
Answer: Each Roman home had a household shrine, known as a lararium, which was a central religious feature. This shrine was used for daily prayers and libations to the family's domestic deities. These deities, often referred to as lares and penates, were believed to protect the household and its members. The household shrine was typically located in a prominent place within the home, often near the entrance or in the atrium, and it served as a focal point for the family's religious practices and daily rituals.

### References

- [1] Roman religion was thus practical and contractual, based on the principle of do ut des, "I give that you might give." Religion depended on knowledge and the correct practice of prayer, ritual, and sacrifice, not on faith or dogma, although Latin literature preserves learned speculation on the nature of the divine and its relation to human affairs. Even the most skeptical among Rome's intellectual elite such as Cicero, who was an augur, saw religion as a source of social order. For ordinary Romans, religion was a part of daily life. Each home had a household shrine at which prayers and libations to the family's domestic deities were offered. Neighborhood shrines and sacred places such as springs and groves dotted the city. The Roman calendar was structured around religious observances. Women, slaves, and children all participated in a range of religious activities. Some public rituals could be conducted only by women, and women formed what is perhaps Rome's most famous priesthood, the state-supported Vestals, who tended Rome's sacred hearth for centuries, until disbanded under Christian domination.

### References

At the start of 1971, Pope Paul VI set the number of cardinal electors at a maximum of 120, but set no limit on the number of cardinals generally. He also established a maximum age of eighty years for electors. His action deprived twenty-five living cardinals, including the three living cardinals elevated by Pope Pius XI, of the right to participate in a conclave.

However, the state experiences a variety of climates due to its geographical diversity. Specifically, Oklahoma has a transition zone between humid continental climate to the north, semi-arid climate to the west, and humid subtropical climate in the central, south, and eastern portions of the state. Q: What unique electoral power does this German high court possess?
Gold: the power and authority to outlaw political parties
Answer: The Bundesverfassungsgericht (Federal Constitutional Court) holds a unique position as the highest German court, responsible for interpreting and amending the German Constitution, the Grundgesetz. One of its distinctive powers is the ability to declare both federal and state legislation ineffective if it violates the Constitution. Additionally, the Federal Constitutional Court has the authority to overrule decisions made by other federal courts, despite not being a regular court of appeals in the German court system. Perhaps most notably, this court has the power to outlaw political parties that repeatedly violate articles of the Constitution.

### References

- [1] Final interpretation of and amendments to the German Constitution, the Grundgesetz, is the task of the Bundesverfassungsgericht (Federal Constitutional Court), which is the de facto highest German court, as it can declare both federal and state legislation ineffective, and has the power to overrule decisions of all other federal courts, despite not being a regular court of appeals on itself in the German court system. It is also the only court possessing the power and authority to outlaw political parties, if it is deemed that these parties have repeatedly violated articles of the Constitution.

Q: Many instruments originated during what era?
Gold: the Renaissance
Answer: Many instruments originated during the Renaissance era. During this period, various types of instruments such as brass, stringed, percussion, and woodwind instruments emerged or were improved upon. For instance, brass instruments like the slide trumpet, wooden cornet, valveless trumpet, and sackbut were traditionally played by members of Guilds. Stringed instruments included the viol, harp-like lyre, hurdy-gurdy, cittern, and lute. Keyboard instruments with strings were represented by the harpsichord and virginal. Percussion instruments such as the triangle, Jew's harp, tambourine, bells, rumble-pot, and various kinds of drums were also common. These instruments played a significant role in the musical landscape of the Renaissance.

### References

- [1] Many instruments originated during the Renaissance; others were variations of, or improvements upon, instruments that had existed previously. Some have survived to the present day; others have disappeared, only to be recreated in order to perform music of the period on authentic instruments.
- [2] Brass instruments in the Renaissance were traditionally played by professionals who were members of Guilds and they included the slide trumpet, the wooden cornet, the valveless trumpet and the sackbut. Stringed instruments included the viol, the harp-like lyre, the hurdy-gurdy, the cittern and the lute. Keyboard instruments with strings included the harpsichord and the virginal. Percussion instruments include the triangle, the Jew's harp, the tambourine, the bells, the rumble-pot, and various kinds of drums. Woodwind instruments included the double reed shawm, the reed pipe, the bagpipe, the transverse flute and the recorder.

- **Plato (c. 428/427–c. 348/347 BC)**: A student of Socrates, Plato is a canonical figure in the field of philosophy. He founded the Platonic Academy and produced systematic discussions of natural philosophy, including metaphysics, ethics, politics, and logic. His works, such as *The Republic* and *Phaedo*, have had a profound impact on Western philosophy.

- **Aristotle (384–322 BC)**: A student of Plato, Aristotle is also a canonical figure in the field of philosophy. He is known for his contributions to various disciplines, including metaphysics, ethics, politics, and logic. Aristotle believed that no void could occur naturally due to the denser surrounding material continuum filling any incipient rarity. This belief reflects his understanding of the physical world and the interdependence of its components. He also introduced empiricism and the notion that universal truths can be arrived at via observation and induction, thereby laying the foundations of the scientific method.

- **Socrates (c. 470–399 BC)**: A historical philosopher who has become a canonical figure in the field of philosophy. Socrates is known for his method of questioning and his contributions to ethics and epistemology. Although he wrote nothing, his ideas were recorded by his students, most notably Plato.

- **Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD)**: A Christian philosopher and theologian, Augustine is a canonical figure in the field of philosophy. He is known for his contributions to the rule of law and his philosophical arguments, such as those presented in *Confessions* and *City of God*.

- **Descartes (1596–1650)**: A historical philosopher who has become a canonical figure in the field of philosophy. Descartes is known for his quest for certainty and his method of doubt, which laid the foundation for modern philosophy. His works, such as *Meditations on First Philosophy*, have had a significant impact on the development of Western philosophy.

These philosophers have left a lasting legacy and continue to be studied and debated in academic circles. Their ideas have influenced various fields, including ethics, politics, metaphysics, and epistemology.

Q: Atomically, glass is similar to what?
Gold: a supercooled liquid
Answer: Atomically, glass is similar to a supercooled liquid. Both exhibit characteristics of a liquid at the atomic level but remain in a solid state below their respective transition temperatures. This means that while the atoms in glass are arranged in a disordered manner, akin to a liquid, they do not have enough energy to rearrange into a crystalline structure, thus maintaining a solid form.

### References

- [1] Although the atomic structure of glass shares characteristics of the structure in a supercooled liquid, glass tends to behave as a solid below its glass transition temperature. A supercooled liquid behaves as a liquid, but it is below the freezing point of the material, and in some cases will crystallize almost instantly if a crystal is added as a core. The change in heat capacity at a glass transition and a melting transition of comparable materials are typically of the same order of magnitude, indicating that the change in active degrees of freedom is comparable as well. Both in a glass and in a crystal it is mostly only the vibrational degrees of freedom that remain active, whereas rotational and translational motion is arrested. This helps to explain why both crystalline and non-crystalline solids exhibit rigidity on most experimental time scales.

At more or less the same time the Ingvaeonic nasal spirant law led to the development of Old Saxon, Old Frisian (Anglo-Frisian) and Old English (Anglo-Saxon). Hardly influenced by either development, Old Dutch remained close to the original language of the Franks, the people that would rule Europe for centuries. The language however, did experienced developments on its own, like final-obstruent devoicing in a very early stage. In fact, by judging from the find at Bergakker, it would seem that the language already experienced this characteristic during the Old Frankish period.

#703
Q: What does Mexico City rest on?
Gold: Lake Texcoco
Answer: Mexico City primarily rests on what was Lake Texcoco. The lake was drained starting from the 17th century, and the city now sits on the lake bed's heavily saturated clay. This soft base has led to significant subsidence issues, with some areas of the city having sunk as much as nine meters (30 feet) since the beginning of the 20th century. This subsidence has caused problems with runoff and wastewater management, leading to flooding problems, especially during the rainy season.

### References

- [1] Mexico city primarily rests on what was Lake Texcoco. Seismic activity is frequent here. Lake Texcoco was drained starting from the 17th century. Although none of the lake waters remain, the city rests on the lake bed's heavily saturated clay. This soft base is collapsing due to the over-extraction of groundwater, called groundwater-related subsidence. Since the beginning of the 20th century the city has sunk as much as nine metres (30 feet) in some areas. This sinking is causing problems with runoff and wastewater management, leading to flooding problems, especially during the rainy season. The entire lake bed is now paved over and most of the city's remaining forested areas lie in the southern boroughs of Milpa Alta, Tlalpan and Xochimilco.

#715
Q: Following the Carolingian unification, the term Ashkenazi came to refer to the Jews of what two places?
Gold: medieval Germany and France
Answer: Following the Carolingian unification, the term Ashkenazi came to refer to the Jews of medieval Germany and France. This terminology arose as the Jewish communities in these regions developed their own customs, language, and traditions, distinct from those in other areas.

### References

- [1] Sometime in the early medieval period, the Jews of central and eastern Europe came to be called by this term. In conformity with the custom of designating areas of Jewish settlement with biblical names, Spain was denominated Sefarad (Obadiah 20), France was called Tsarefat (1 Kings 17:9), and Bohemia was called the Land of Canaan. By the high medieval period, Talmudic commentators like Rashi began to use Ashkenaz/Eretz Ashkenaz to designate Germany, earlier known as Loter, where, especially in the Rhineland communities of Speyer, Worms and Mainz, the most important Jewish communities arose. Rashi uses leshon Ashkenaz (Ashkenazi language) to describe German speech, and Byzantium and Syrian Jewish letters referred to the Crusaders as Ashkenazim. Given the close links between the Jewish communities of France and Germany following the Carolingian unification, the term Ashkenazi came to refer to both the Jews of medieval Germany and France.

#716
Q: The term "antigen" is rooted in what two words?
Gold: "anti"body "gen"erators
Answer: The term "antigen" is derived from the words "anti" and "gen," which together indicate its role in eliciting the generation of antibodies. Specifically, "anti" refers to the concept of opposition or resistance, while "gen" relates to the production or generation. Thus, antigens are defined as anything that elicits the generation of antibodies.

### References

- [1] The humoral (antibody) response is defined as the interaction between antibodies and antigens. Antibodies are specific proteins released from a certain class of immune cells known as B lymphocytes, while antigens are defined as anything that elicits the generation of antibodies (\"anti\"body \"gen\"erators). Immunology rests on an understanding of the properties of these two biological entities and the cellular response to both.

#738
Q: What is database storage?
Gold: physical materialization of a database
Answer: Database storage is the container for the physical materialization of a database. It comprises the internal (physical) level in the database architecture and contains all the information needed to reconstruct the conceptual level and external level from the internal level when required. This includes metadata, or "data about the data," and internal data structures. The database engine, also known as the "storage engine," is responsible for putting data into permanent storage within the database storage.

### References

- [1] Database storage is the container of the physical materialization of a database. It comprises the internal (physical) level in the database architecture. It also contains all the information needed (e.g., metadata, "data about the data," and internal data structures) to reconstruct the conceptual level and external level from the internal level when needed. Putting data into permanent storage is generally the responsibility of the database engine a.k.a. "storage engine". Though typically accessed by a DBMS through the underlying operating system (and often utilizing the operating systems' file systems as intermediates for storage layout), storage properties and configuration setting are extremely important for the efficient operation of the DBMS, and thus are closely maintained by database administrators. A DBMS, while in operation, always has its database residing in several types of storage (e.g., memory and external storage). The database data and the additional needed information, possibly in very large amounts, are coded into bits. Data typically reside in the storage in structures that look completely different from the way the data look in the conceptual and external levels, but in ways that attempt to optimize (the best possible) these levels' reconstruction when needed by users and programs, as well as for computing additional types of needed information from the data (e.g., when querying the database).

Q: What is a commonly seen example?
Gold: double happiness symbol
Answer: A commonly seen example is the **apple**. In philosophical discussions, the apple is often used to illustrate the distinction between **primary qualities** and **secondary qualities**. Primary qualities are essential for the object to be what it is, such as its atomic structure, which defines it as an apple. Secondary qualities, on the other hand, are sensory information derived from these primary qualities, like its color, size, and texture. This example helps in understanding how an object can be identified based on its intrinsic properties (primary qualities) and the perceptions we have of it (secondary qualities).

### References

- [1] In response to the early-to-mid-17th century "continental rationalism" John Locke (1632–1704) proposed in An Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1689) a very influential view wherein the only knowledge humans can have is a posteriori, i.e., based upon experience. Locke is famously attributed with holding the proposition that the human mind is a tabula rasa, a "blank tablet", in Locke's words "white paper", on which the experiences derived from sense impressions as a person's life proceeds are written. There are two sources of our ideas: sensation and reflection. In both cases, a distinction is made between simple and complex ideas. The former are unanalysable, and are broken down into primary and secondary qualities. Primary qualities are essential for the object in question to be what it is. Without specific primary qualities, an object would not be what it is. For example, an apple is an apple because of the arrangement of its atomic structure. If an apple was structured differently, it would cease to be an apple. Secondary qualities are the sensory information we can perceive from its primary qualities. For example, an apple can be perceived in various colours, sizes, and textures but it is still identified as an apple. Therefore, its primary qualities dictate what the object essentially is, while its secondary qualities define its attributes. Complex ideas combine simple ones, and divide into substances, modes, and relations. According to Locke, our knowledge of things is a perception of ideas that are in accordance or discordance with each other, which is very different from the quest for certainty of Descartes.

Q: At the time change to DST, what will a digital clock read just after 01:59:59.9?
Gold: 03:00:00.0
Answer: Just after 01:59:59.9 during the transition to Daylight Saving Time (DST), a digital clock will jump to 03:00:00.0. This occurs because the clock jumps forward one hour at 02:00 local time, effectively skipping the hour from 02:00 to 03:00. Therefore, the digital display will not read 02:00 at all; instead, it will directly show 03:00:00.0.

### References

- [1] In the case of the United States where a one-hour shift occurs at 02:00 local time, in spring the clock jumps forward from the last moment of 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST and that day has 23 hours, whereas in autumn the clock jumps backward from the last moment of 01:59 DST to 01:00 standard time, repeating that hour, and that day has 25 hours. A digital display of local time does not read 02:00 exactly at the shift to summer time, but instead jumps from 01:59:59.9 forward to 03:00:00.0.

Q: Are Safe Harbor agreements and ITPs mutually exclusive?
Gold: A landowner can have either a "Safe Harbor" agreement or an Incidental Take Permit, or both.
Answer: Safe Harbor agreements and Incidental Take Permits (ITPs) are not mutually exclusive. A landowner can have both a Safe Harbor Agreement and an ITP. The Safe Harbor Agreement focuses on benefiting or attracting listed or proposed species, while the ITP allows for the incidental taking of listed species within certain limits. These agreements can coexist, providing landowners with assurances for future "takes" under the Safe Harbor Agreement and specific permission for incidental takings under the ITP.

### References

- [1] The "Safe Harbor" agreement is a voluntary agreement between the private landowner and FWS. The landowner agrees to alter the property to benefit or even attract a listed or proposed species in exchange for assurances that the FWS will permit future "takes" above a pre-determined level. A landowner can have either a "Safe Harbor" agreement or an Incidental Take Permit, or both. The policy was developed by the Clinton Administration in 1999.
- [2] The person or organization submits a HCP and if approved by the agency (FWS or NMFS), will be issued an Incidental Take Permit (ITP) which allows a certain number of "takes" of the listed species. The permit may be revoked at any time and can allow incidental takes for varying amounts of time. For instance, the San Bruno Habitat Conservation Plan/ Incidental Take Permit is good for 30 years and the Wal-Mart store (in Florida) permit expires after one year. Because the permit is issued by a federal agency to a private party, it is a federal action-which means other federal laws can apply, such as the National Environmental Policy Act or NEPA. A notice of the permit application action is published in the Federal Register and a public comment period of 30 to 90 days begins.

Q: What was the real number of people that took part in the plebiscite that passed Napoleon's constitution?
Gold: 1.5 million
Answer: The real number of people who participated in the plebiscite that passed Napoleon's Constitution of the Year VIII was 1.5 million, as reported by Lucien, Napoleon's brother, who falsified the returns to show a higher participation rate. However, political observers at the time estimated that the eligible French voting public numbered about 5 million people, so the regime artificially doubled the participation rate to indicate popular enthusiasm for the Consulate.

### References

- [1] Napoleon established a political system that historian Martyn Lyons called "dictatorship by plebiscite." Worried by the democratic forces unleashed by the Revolution, but unwilling to ignore them entirely, Napoleon resorted to regular electoral consultations with the French people on his road to imperial power. He drafted the Constitution of the Year VIII and secured his own election as First Consul, taking up residence at the Tuileries. The constitution was approved in a rigged plebiscite held the following January, with 99.94 percent officially listed as voting "yes." Napoleon's brother, Lucien, had falsified the returns to show that 3 million people had participated in the plebiscite; the real number was 1.5 million. Political observers at the time assumed the eligible French voting public numbered about 5 million people, so the regime artificially doubled the participation rate to indicate popular enthusiasm for the Consulate. In the first few months of the Consulate, with war in Europe still raging and internal instability still plaguing the country, Napoleon's grip on power remained very tenuous.

This unique political structure meant that the king's estates were managed according to the interests of the nobility, but the nobility did not have direct control over them.

### References

Despite having a king, Poland was called the nobility's Commonwealth because the king was elected by all interested members of hereditary nobility and Poland was considered to be the property of this class, not of the king or the ruling dynasty. This state of affairs grew up in part because of the extinction of the male-line descendants of the old royal dynasty (first the Piasts, then the Jagiellons), and the selection by the nobility of their king from among the dynasty's female-line descendants.

Q: At DST in the fall, how long does it stay the same time in both Pacific and Mountain time in the United States?
Gold: one hour
Answer: In the fall when Daylight Saving Time (DST) ends, the clocks in the Pacific and Mountain time zones are set back to Standard Time. At the moment the clocks are set back, which is typically at 02:00 local time, the time remains the same for one hour. Specifically, the time jumps from 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST, effectively skipping the 02:00 hour. This means that for one hour, the time is effectively the same as 03:00, creating a unique situation where the day has 25 hours.

### References

- [1] In the case of the United States where a one-hour shift occurs at 02:00 local time, in spring the clock jumps forward from the last moment of 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST and that day has 23 hours, whereas in autumn the clock jumps backward from the last moment of 01:59 DST to 01:00 standard time, repeating that hour, and that day has 25 hours. A digital display of local time does not read 02:00 exactly at the shift to summer time, but instead jumps from 01:59:59.9 forward to 03:00:00.0.

#840
Q: If the plate area and separation distance are altered while keeping the amount of dielectric the same, what effect is had on the maximum energy of the capacitor?
Gold: no change of the maximum amount of energy
Answer: When the plate area and separation distance are altered while maintaining the same amount of dielectric, the maximum energy stored in the capacitor remains unchanged. This is because the maximum energy \( W \) that a capacitor can store is given by the formula:

\[ W = \frac{1}{2} C V^2 \]

where \( C \) is the capacitance and \( V \) is the voltage across the capacitor. The capacitance \( C \) of a parallel-plate capacitor is determined by the equation:

\[ C = \frac{\epsilon A}{d} \]

Here, \( \epsilon \) is the permittivity of the dielectric, \( A \) is the plate area, and \( d \) is the separation between the plates. Since the dielectric volume remains constant, the product \( \epsilon A \) and the ratio \( \frac{A}{d} \) are adjusted to maintain the same capacitance \( C \). Consequently, the maximum energy stored in the capacitor does not change, as long as the distance between the plates remains much smaller than both the length and width of the plates.

### References

- [1] The maximum energy is a function of dielectric volume, permittivity, and dielectric strength.
Score: 5.0 | Pass: True

Q: How can the speed of larger brushes be increased?
Gold: Stiffer brush springs
Answer: The speed of larger brushes can be increased by using stiffer brush springs. While this approach improves the speed, it comes with the trade-off of reduced efficiency and increased wear on both the brushes and the commutator. This is because stiffer springs can better manage the increased contact area and motor output, but at the cost of higher friction losses and accelerated wear.

### References

- [1] Large brushes are desired for a larger brush contact area to maximize motor output, but small brushes are desired for low mass to maximize the speed at which the motor can run without the brushes excessively bouncing and sparking. (Small brushes are also desirable for lower cost.) Stiffer brush springs can also be used to make brushes of a given mass work at a higher speed, but at the cost of greater friction losses (lower efficiency) and accelerated brush and commutator wear. Therefore, DC motor brush design entails a trade-off between output power, speed, and efficiency/wear.

Answer: The mathematical statement of computers' versatility is known as the Church–Turing thesis. This thesis states that any computer with a minimum capability (being Turing-complete) is, in principle, capable of performing the same tasks that any other computer can perform. Therefore, any type of computer (netbook, supercomputer, cellular automaton, etc.) is able to perform the same computational tasks, given enough time and storage capacity.

- [1] Church–Turing Thesis

Q: How high of a temperature change can glass-ceramics handle?
Gold: 1000 °C
Answer: Glass-ceramics can sustain repeated and quick temperature changes up to 1000 °C, making them suitable for applications requiring frequent and significant temperature fluctuations. This property is due to their unique structure, which balances the negative thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) of the crystalline ceramic phase with the positive CTE of the glassy phase, resulting in a net CTE near zero at a certain crystallinity level (~70% crystalline).

### References

- [1] The term mainly refers to a mix of lithium and aluminosilicates that yields an array of materials with interesting thermomechanical properties. The most commercially important of these have the distinction of being impervious to thermal shock. Thus, glass-ceramics have become extremely useful for countertop cooking. The negative thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) of the crystalline ceramic phase can be balanced with the positive CTE of the glassy phase. At a certain point (~70% crystalline) the glass-ceramic has a net CTE near zero. This type of glass-ceramic exhibits excellent mechanical properties and can sustain repeated and quick temperature changes up to 1000 °C.

#917
Q: What are the natural theories of law that that the English judges in the eighteenth century used?
Gold: law was believed to have an existence independent of what individual judges said
Answer: The English judges in the eighteenth century subscribed to now-obsolete natural law theories of law. These theories posited that law had an existence independent of what individual judges said, and judges saw themselves as merely declaring the law that had always theoretically existed, rather than making the law. This perspective influenced their approach to judicial decisions, where they could reject another judge's opinion as an incorrect statement of the law, similar to how scientists might reject each other's conclusions as incorrect statements of scientific laws.

### References

- [1] Canonical jurisprudential theory generally follows the principles of Aristotelian-Thomistic legal philosophy. While the term "law" is never explicitly defined in the Code, the Catechism of the Catholic Church cites Aquinas in defining law as "...an ordinance of reason for the common good, promulgated by the one who is in charge of the community" and reformulates it as "...a rule of conduct enacted by competent authority for the sake of the common good."

#953
Q: What usually changes when a place observes DST?
Gold: The name of local time
Answer: When a place observes Daylight Saving Time (DST), several changes occur, primarily related to the adjustment of local time. Typically, clocks are moved forward by one hour at the start of DST, and backward by one hour at the end of DST. This adjustment can affect various aspects of daily life and technology.

For instance, in the spring, the clock jumps forward from the last moment of 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST, meaning that the day has 23 hours instead of the usual 24. Conversely, in the autumn, the clock jumps backward from the last moment of 01:59 DST to 01:00 standard time, causing that hour to repeat, and the day has 25 hours. During these transitions, digital displays do not read 02:00 exactly at the shift to summer time; instead, they jump from 01:59:59.9 to 03:00:00.0.

These changes can impact various systems and devices. For example, a computer timing system that relies on a radio time synchronization signal might experience issues if not properly adjusted. In one notable incident, a German steel facility suffered damage due to a computer timing system that allowed molten steel to cool for one hour less than required, leading to spattering of molten steel when it was poured.

Additionally, software developers and consumers must update their systems and devices to reflect the correct DST rules. This includes updating programmable thermostats and other devices that rely on accurate timekeeping. To avoid issues related to local time zones, Unix-based computer systems often use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) internally.

- [1] Document Title One
- [2] Document Title Two
